title: Each Board column scrolls on its own and technicians are never hidden
custom_preconds:
1. Sign in to the build under test as a user whose role has Work Orders view (check in Settings > Roles & Permissions > open your role > Work Orders section). The Admin role has both.
  2. Use a desktop browser with the window at least 1024 pixels wide (full screen on an ordinary laptop or monitor). Below that width the page shows only List.
  3. In the top bar, choose the location you will test in (e.g. "Heavy Duty"). Create everything below in this location.
  4. Make sure the location has the technicians this case uses (e.g. at least 8 technicians). A person only counts as a technician here when the staff record is Active, Clockable is on, the role is neither Office nor Time Clock User, and they are enrolled at this location. To add one:
    • Settings > Staff > add a staff member > enter the first and last name (e.g. Esther Howard), role Technician, Clockable on, Active, enrolled at this location > Save.
  5. Create the work orders this case uses and set their lead technician (about 25 with no lead, about 20 led by Esther Howard, a few for each other technician):
    • Work Orders > New Work Order > choose a customer (e.g. "Fibridge Commercial") and an asset (e.g. unit TRK-118, 2022 Freightliner M2) > Create. Write down the number the build gives the work order (the numbers in this case are examples).
    • On the work order page set Lead Technician (e.g. Esther Howard) and save. Leave Lead Technician empty on the ones that should sit in Unassigned.
custom_steps:
1. Open Work Orders.
  2. Click the All tab on the left of the toolbar.
  3. In the display switcher at the right of the toolbar, click Board View (in the design its tooltip reads "Board").
  4. Scroll down inside the Unassigned column.
  5. Watch the neighbouring columns and the headers.
  6. Try to scroll the whole page down with the mouse over the empty area below a short column.
  7. Scroll down inside Esther Howard's column.
  8. Scroll the board sideways to the far right and back.
  9. Count the technician columns you passed.
custom_expected:
Expected results

  • Scrolling inside Unassigned moves only its cards: the next columns and every header stay where they are.
  • The page itself does not scroll down: only the content inside a column scrolls.
  • Esther Howard's column scrolls on its own the same way.
  • Sideways scrolling reaches every technician: the number of technician columns equals the number of eligible technicians (e.g. 8). None is hidden automatically.

Source — where this behaviour comes from
Epic SV-10043; story SV-10046 (Story 3, Board View — board by lead technician); PRD Confluence 845185030, edited 7 Oct 2026 (status line "PRD v33"), S3-E1, S3-E2, read 8 Oct 2026. Review Decisions 853901313 UX-11 / DR-40. PRD inline comment Branko Cicovic 28 Sep 2026 (only content inside the columns scrolls).

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

  • S3-E1: “Every Board View column, including Unassigned, scrolls vertically on its own when its cards exceed the available viewport, while adjacent columns and pinned headers remain visible. The page itself does not scroll vertically; only the content inside each column does.”
  • S3-E2: “Allow horizontal scrolling when technician columns exceed the available viewport; never hide technicians automatically.”
